title: How to Use Spin the Wheel: Lists, Imports, Styles, and Results
intro: A practical walkthrough of the Classic wheel, from preparing a clean option list and importing Excel data to adjusting individual items, styling the stage, and saving results.
author: Spinanywheel Team
imageAlt: Current Spin the Wheel Classic editor with Options on the left, wheel in the center, and Look controls on the right

seo.title: How to Use Spin the Wheel - Spin the Wheel Blog
seo.description: Learn Spin the Wheel setup with Spinanywheel: prepare options, import Excel data, change weights and colors, style the wheel, spin, and export Results.
keywords: how to use spin the wheel

detailsHtml:
Classic mode is the right starting point when one list needs one random answer at a time: a student name, a dinner choice, a game prompt, a country, or a team. The page is arranged around the way a real session is prepared. Options and Results are on the left, the live wheel stays in the center, and Look, Chrome, and Stage controls are on the right. This guide follows that order so you can build a useful wheel without opening every setting.

Start by deciding what one spin should answer

Write the question before writing the list. “Which film will we watch?” produces a clearer wheel than mixing films, snacks, and start times in the same Options list. Every visible item should be an answer the group is prepared to accept. Remove placeholders, accidental duplicates, and choices that are no longer available before anyone sees the wheel spin.

Classic mode treats each spin as a choice from the current Options list. Keep Remove winner off when the same option may appear again, such as repeated drawing prompts. Turn it on when you are allocating unique countries, classroom turns, or tasks and each selected item should leave the wheel.

Add, edit, sort, or shuffle Options

Open the Options tab on the left. You can add an item, edit its label in place, delete it, sort the list, or shuffle the current order. The editor supports up to 100 options and keeps each label to 36 characters. Short labels are easier to read on the wheel, especially when the list contains more than a dozen items.

Current Classic option limits
InputSupported valuePractical advice
Wheel optionsUp to 100Use smaller focused lists when labels need to be read across a room
Option labelUp to 36 charactersPrefer a short display name over a full description
Item weight1–100Leave all values at 1 for equal chances
Session historyUp to 1,000 spinsDownload CSV before clearing an important session

The percentage shown beside each item is more useful than the raw weight. With six equal items, each displays about 16.7%. If one item is duplicated, that outcome now occupies two option records and can be selected twice as often as a single matching-weight item. Delete the duplicate unless that extra chance is intentional.

Paste a list or import an Excel column

Select Import when typing each option would be slower. Paste accepts one option per line and also separates values at commas, semicolons, or tabs. Review the preview count, then choose Add to wheel to keep the current list or Replace wheel to start clean.

For Excel, choose a .xlsx or .xls workbook no larger than 5 MB. The importer reads the workbook in the browser, lets you select a worksheet and one column, and turns every non-empty cell in that column into an option. A reliable sheet looks like this:

Recommended Excel layout for Options
Column AImport?
Alex KimYes
Jordan LeeYes
Sam RiveraYes
Participant nameDelete this header from the preview or sheet

Keep unrelated notes, email addresses, eligibility status, and prize information in other columns and import only the public label. The wheel is a display surface, so avoid exposing personal data that participants did not agree to show.

Use Advanced only when one item needs different treatment

Advanced lets you change an individual option's weight, background color, text color, and image. Equal weights are the clearest choice when players expect equal odds. If you deliberately use different weights, show the displayed percentages before spinning. The actual chance is the item's weight divided by the total of all item weights; a weight of 50 is not automatically a 50% chance.

Item images are useful for flags, icons, or simple visual prompts. Keep text contrast readable and do not rely on color alone to identify an outcome. Uploaded images are processed in the browser, must be image files, and are limited to 5 MB before processing.

Style the wheel without changing its data

The right side separates appearance into three groups. Look changes slice geometry and can add a wheel-face image. Chrome controls the pointer style and position, rim, and lights. Stage changes the background and winner scene. These controls do not alter the option labels or their probabilities.

Choose style for the room rather than for the settings panel. A projector benefits from high-contrast labels, a simple stage, and a clear pointer. A party or stream can use a brighter rim and winner scene. Uploading a background can make the page feel specific to an event, but check that it does not compete with the wheel text.

Check sound, timing, fullscreen, and sharing

The toolbar above the wheel provides sound, fullscreen, sharing, style access, spin settings, history, and reset. Spin settings control duration and audio choices. Shorter timing is useful for repeated classroom turns; a longer spin can build anticipation during an event. Reduced-motion browser preferences shorten the animation automatically.

Share copies the current wheel setup into a link. It is useful when another person needs the same option list and settings. It does not serve as a results archive. Do not treat the shared URL as proof of who was selected; download the session results for that purpose.

Spin and read the result in the Results panel

Press the center Spin button after everyone has seen the final list and repeat rule. The result is selected first, then the animation is calculated to stop inside the corresponding slice. When the spin finishes, the winner appears in Results and the session history updates.

View all rounds opens the fuller session summary. It shows the number of rounds, how many options have been picked, participation counts, and the recorded sequence. CSV export contains round, queueItem, queueTurn, entry, runMode, and pickedAt. In Classic mode, the two Queue fields stay empty.

A complete Classic workflow

  1. State the one question the wheel will answer.
  2. Add or import only acceptable answers.
  3. Check the option count, duplicates, labels, and displayed chances.
  4. Choose whether Remove winner should be on.
  5. Adjust item appearance in Advanced only where needed.
  6. Set Look, Chrome, Stage, sound, and timing for the room.
  7. Show the finished list, spin, and read the result card.
  8. Open all rounds and download CSV if the sequence matters.

Use the Spin The Wheel Yes Or No, Europe Country Wheel, or Color Spin The Wheel when a prepared list is faster than starting blank. If the activity needs ordered people, teams, or prize tiers with a fixed number of turns, continue with the Turn Queue guide.

How this guide was checked

The steps, labels, import formats, limits, and result fields were checked against the current Options importer, Advanced controls, style panels, session summary, and CSV formatter on August 12, 2026. The wheel is intended for classrooms, games, everyday decisions, and informal events. It is not a certified lottery or gambling system.

title: How to Use Turn Queue for Prize Draws and Group Rounds
intro: Learn the difference between Options and Queue, then build a multi-prize raffle or repeated group activity with turn counts, Remove winner, live progress, and CSV results.
author: Spinanywheel Team
imageAlt: Current Event Raffle Wheel with participant names, three prize tiers in Turn Queue, and Remove winner enabled

seo.title: How to Use Turn Queue - Spin the Wheel Blog | Spinanywheel
seo.description: Use Spinanywheel Turn Queue for prize draws, teams, or classroom rounds. Learn where names go, how turn counts work, when to remove winners, and export Results.

detailsHtml:
Turn Queue is for sessions that need more structure than “spin again.” It keeps a second ordered list beside the wheel and gives every Queue item a turn count. In an event raffle, participant names belong in Options while prize tiers belong in Queue. In a classroom game, prompts can stay in Options while students or teams and their allowed turns go in Queue. Keeping those two jobs separate is the key to using the mode correctly.

Options and Queue hold different data

Options are the labels the wheel can select. Queue tells the site which person, team, prize, or round is currently active and how many spins it receives. The Now Playing card repeats the active Queue label above the wheel, and the progress panel shows completed turns and what comes next.

Where each kind of data belongs
ScenarioOptionsQueue
Company prize drawEligible participant names3rd prize ×3, 2nd prize ×2, 1st prize ×1
Classroom turnsQuestions, topics, or tasksStudent names with their turn counts
Team challengeChallenges or point valuesTeam Red ×3, Team Blue ×3
Game draftRoles, types, or itemsPlayer or roster slots

Do not put names and prizes together on the wheel for a multi-prize event. A result such as “Alex Kim” answers who won, while the highlighted Queue item answers what they won. Combining both sets into Options can land on a prize name instead of a participant.

Build the Event Raffle setup

The Event Raffle Wheel starts with eight sample names and three Queue items: third prize for three turns, second prize for two, and first prize for one. Replace the sample names in Options with the eligible participant list. Then edit the Queue labels and turn counts so they match the real prizes.

  1. Open Turn Queue mode.
  2. Put participant names in Options.
  3. Put the lower prize tier first if that is your published draw order.
  4. Set each Queue turn count to the number of winners needed for that tier.
  5. Enable Remove winner when one participant may win only once.
  6. Confirm that the total no-repeat turns do not exceed the number of Options.

In the starter setup, 3 + 2 + 1 creates six scheduled spins. Eight names are enough to complete all six with Remove winner on, leaving two unselected participants. If you schedule ten no-repeat prizes but load only eight names, the wheel will run out of eligible options before Queue is finished.

Add Queue items manually or import them

Select Add item for a short Queue. Each label is limited to 36 characters, and each item accepts 1 to 99 turns. The current Queue supports up to 200 items, although a shorter visible sequence is easier for participants to follow.

The paste importer expects one Queue item per line. Add a comma, tab, or semicolon before the number of turns:

Prize Queue example

3rd prize, 3
2nd prize, 2
1st prize, 1

A line without a number starts at one turn and can be edited later. Excel import accepts .xlsx and .xls files up to 5 MB. Choose one column for the Queue label and an optional second column for turns. The importer attempts to recognize a numeric turns column, but you should check the preview before replacing the Queue.

Choose the correct Remove winner rule

Remove winner applies to the wheel Options, not to Queue items. Turn it on for a raffle where each person may receive only one prize. After a result settles, that person's option is removed, while the active prize tier remains until its assigned turn count is complete.

Leave Remove winner off when Options are repeatable prompts or challenges. For example, Team Red and Team Blue may each receive three turns from Queue while the same task can appear for both teams. State the repeat rule before the first spin so the audience does not assume the wrong behavior.

Understand Queue order and live progress

Queue runs in the order shown. The first incomplete, unskipped item becomes active. If third prize has three turns, the active item stays on third prize until three results have been recorded. The panel then advances to second prize automatically.

Skip current item resolves the active Queue item without using its remaining turns. Use it for an absent player, a cancelled prize, or a round the group has deliberately removed. Reset queue progress starts the Queue sequence over; it should not be pressed halfway through a real draw unless you intend to restart and explain what happens to the earlier records.

Run a multi-prize draw in the room

  1. Display the final participant count and Queue order.
  2. Explain eligibility, duplicate-name handling, Remove winner, redraws, and absences.
  3. Confirm the Now Playing card names the correct prize.
  4. Spin once, read the winner, and wait for the result to record.
  5. Verify the tier progress before the next spin.
  6. Continue until Queue reports that all available turns are complete.
  7. Open all rounds and download the session CSV.

Drawing lower prizes first is common when first prize should be selected from people who did not already win, but it is not automatically the correct order for every event. Match the Queue to the rules you announced. Changing the order after seeing an outcome damages trust more than any visual setting can repair.

Use Results to verify the finished sequence

Turn Queue Results records each selected entry together with the Queue label and turn number. The session summary shows Queue rounds, unique picks, resolved Queue items, per-item progress, participation counts, and the round list. CSV export contains six columns:

Turn Queue CSV fields
FieldMeaning
roundResult order in the current session
queueItemPrize, player, team, or round active for the result
queueTurnIts turn number within that Queue item
entryThe option selected by the wheel
runModeturn-queue
pickedAtISO timestamp recorded when the spin completed

The CSV is useful for distributing classroom assignments or keeping an informal event record. It does not include eligibility evidence, identity verification, deleted names, published contest terms, or an independent audit. Save those separately where the event requires them.

Other Turn Queue patterns

The same structure can handle more than raffles. In the Pokémon Type Team Wheel, the 18 types are Options and six team slots are Queue items. In a classroom elimination activity, student names can be Options while question rounds form the Queue. For a team game, challenges can be Options while each team receives a fixed number of turns.

The question to ask is: “What should the wheel select, and whose or which round is it?” Put the selectable answer in Options and the ordered context in Queue. If there is no ordered context and you only need repeated independent choices, Classic is simpler.

Pre-session checklist

  • Options and Queue have not been reversed.
  • Every participant or selectable item appears once unless duplicates are intentional.
  • Queue labels and turn counts match the actual session.
  • Remove winner matches the repeat rule.
  • Total no-repeat turns do not exceed the number of eligible Options.
  • Draw order, skips, absences, and redraw rules are agreed beforehand.
  • Someone is responsible for downloading Results when the session ends.

For list preparation, Excel column selection, individual option settings, wheel styles, and Classic Results, read How to use Spin the Wheel.

How this guide was checked

The article was checked against the current Turn Queue editor, paste and Excel importers, Queue progression, skip and reset controls, Remove winner behavior, session summary, Event Raffle template, and CSV formatter on August 12, 2026. Turn Queue is intended for classroom, game, group, and informal prize sessions; it does not turn the browser wheel into certified lottery software.
